transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm explaining this okay, but I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble with... just keeping track of things? Like, basic adult things. 

I know everyone gets a little scattered sometimes, right? But I've been forgetting to pay bills, and... well, to be honest, I've missed returning a few emails for job interviews. I feel terrible about it, and I really am trying my best, I promise. But I keep missing appointments and forgetting to follow through on errands, and it's... it's kind of starting to cost me some real opportunities. I just want to get it together, you know? Does that make sense as a reason to be here?
Have you struggled with these kinds of attention and organizational issues since childhood, or is this a more recent change for you?

Um, well... I guess it's been going on for a while? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm making excuses or anything, but... yeah, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always say I was really bright. They always made sure to say that first! But then they'd write on my report cards that I... um, that I kind of lost my worksheets a lot, or that I rushed through directions without reading them all the way. 

And, um, they said I talked out of turn sometimes, too. I just got so excited to share, you know? But my desk was always... well, it was a little cluttered. Okay, it was really messy, to the point where I couldn't always find my assignments when it was time to turn them in. I tried to keep it neat, I really did! I just... I don't know, it's always been a little hard for me. Is that the kind of thing you're looking for?
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have an internal motor that's always running?

Um, well... I guess I do like to stay active? I think it's good to keep busy, right? But, um... yeah, I suppose I do feel that way a little bit. Even without a job right now—which I am applying for things, I promise!—I just sort of... move from one thing to the next all day long. 

Like, I'll go to do the laundry, and then I'm checking emails, and then I'm reorganizing all the tabs on my computer, or just pacing around my apartment, and then I'll start prepping dinner... It really does feel like I just cannot let myself stop. I hope that doesn't sound too chaotic? The only bad part—and I feel a little silly admitting this, because I really do try to get things done—is that even though I'm constantly doing things, none of it actually gets finished. I just keep moving to the next thing. Is that... is that the kind of restlessness you mean?
